questions.question: What are the five basic data types available in Python, as introduced in the lecture?
questions.explanation: The lecture states that Python has five data types: Numbers, String, List, Tuple, and Dictionary.
questions.source: See Lecture 26 (Introduction to Python Programming – Part I) @ 15:50

questions.question: Which keyword is used to define a function in Python?
questions.explanation: A function in Python is defined using the def keyword, followed by the function name and its arguments.
questions.source: See Lecture 26 (Introduction to Python Programming – Part I) @ 19:20

questions.question: In Python's exception handling, which keyword is used to handle an exception raised inside the try block?
questions.explanation: Python uses the try, except and else block structure for exception handling; the except block catches the exception raised in the try block.
questions.source: See Lecture 26 (Introduction to Python Programming – Part I) @ 28:55

questions.question: Which mode of Python's open() function is used to add data to the end of an existing file without erasing its existing content?
questions.explanation: Python supports four basic file modes: r (read), w (write), a (append), and r+ (read and write). The append mode adds new data to the end of the file without deleting existing content.
questions.source: See Lecture 27 (Introduction to Python Programming – Part II) @ 02:55

questions.question: Which Python library, installable via pip, is used for image read/write operations as covered in the lecture?
questions.explanation: PIL (Python Image Library) is used to work with image files. It is installed using 'sudo pip install pillow'; PIL supports up to Python 2.7 while Pillow supports Python 3.x.
questions.source: See Lecture 27 (Introduction to Python Programming – Part II) @ 17:25

questions.question: Which socket_type value is used while creating a TCP/IP socket in Python's socket module?
questions.explanation: A socket is created using socket.socket(socket_family, socket_type, protocol). For a TCP/IP (connection-oriented) socket, socket_family is AF_INET and socket_type is SOCK_STREAM.
questions.source: See Lecture 27 (Introduction to Python Programming – Part II) @ 24:40

questions.question: How many GPIO pins does the Raspberry Pi 3 Model B have, as shown in the specifications table?
questions.explanation: As per the specifications table, the Raspberry Pi 3 Model B, Raspberry Pi 2 Model B, and Raspberry Pi Zero all have 40 GPIO pins.
questions.source: See Lecture 28 (Introduction to Raspberry Pi – Part I) @ 05:10

questions.question: Which of the following is an officially supported operating system for Raspberry Pi mentioned in the lecture?
questions.explanation: Raspbian and NOOBS are the officially supported operating systems for Raspberry Pi. Ubuntu Mate, Snappy Ubuntu Core, Windows 10 Core, Pinet, and RISC OS are examples of third-party operating systems.
questions.source: See Lecture 28 (Introduction to Raspberry Pi – Part I) @ 12:05

questions.question: Raspberry Pi is best described as a:
questions.explanation: The lecture introduces Raspberry Pi as a computer that fits in your palm — a low-cost, single-board computer that is easy to access and use.
questions.source: See Lecture 28 (Introduction to Raspberry Pi – Part I) @ 04:45

questions.question: Which command is used to install the GPIO library on Raspberry Pi before programming the blinking LED example?
questions.explanation: After installing Python development tools using 'sudo apt-get install python-dev', the GPIO library is installed using 'sudo apt-get install python-rpi.gpio'.
questions.source: See Lecture 29 (Introduction to Raspberry Pi – Part II) @ 07:43

questions.question: Where is the CSI camera connector slot located on the Raspberry Pi board?
options: Between the Ethernet port and the HDMI port
Next to the power supply pin
On the underside of the board
questions.explanation: The Raspberry Pi Camera connects through a dedicated CSI slot, which is placed between the Ethernet port and the HDMI port on the board.
questions.source: See Lecture 29 (Introduction to Raspberry Pi – Part II) @ 18:27

questions.question: Which terminal command captures a still image using the Raspberry Pi camera?
questions.explanation: Running 'raspistill -o image.jpg' in the terminal captures an image using the Raspberry Pi camera and stores it as image.jpg.
questions.source: See Lecture 29 (Introduction to Raspberry Pi – Part II) @ 19:35

questions.question: What does DHT stand for in the DHT sensor used with Raspberry Pi in the auto-cooling system?
questions.explanation: DHT stands for Digital Humidity and Temperature Sensor. It has 4 pins: PIN 1 (3.3V–5V power supply), PIN 2 (Data), PIN 3 (Null), and PIN 4 (Ground).
questions.source: See Lecture 30 (Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi – Part I) @ 05:20

questions.question: How many output terminals does the relay used in the temperature-dependent auto-cooling system have, as shown in the lecture?
questions.explanation: The relay is a mechanical/electromechanical switch with 3 output terminals (left to right): NO (normal open), Common, and NC (normal close).
questions.source: See Lecture 30 (Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi – Part I) @ 07:50

questions.question: State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: In the temperature-dependent auto-cooling system, the fan operates when the surrounding temperature rises above the threshold value specified in the code.
questions.explanation: The lecture demonstrates that the fan is switched on whenever the measured temperature exceeds the threshold value set in the program.
questions.source: See Lecture 30 (Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi – Part I) @ 18:14
